newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland lifts VAT on insurance brokers' commissions.
newsitem.headline: Poland lifts VAT on insurance brokers' commissions.

text.p: Poland has lifted the seven-percent value-added-tax (VAT) on insurance brokers' and agents' commissions as of January 1, a finance ministry official said on Thursday.
"The VAT on agents' and brokers' commissions has been lifted," Anatol Adamski, head of the ministry's insurance department told Reuters.
Brokers' and agents' commissions amount to between five and 20 percent of the insurance premium.
Adamski said the move would likely cut costs of insurance firms but said it was difficult to say whether it would depress insurance prices.

Insurer TUiR Warta's spokesman Jacek Likowski said the firm was analysing the consequences of the tax move, but said any premium price movements were unlikely as the tax effectively amounted to between 0.35 and 1.4 percent of the whole premium.
"We are analysing the matter, but...it's not very likely that any insurance tariffs will change," he said.
